candidates.predicted_moa: Wnt/β-catenin signaling inhibitor via Axin stabilization and GSK3β-mediated β-catenin phosphorylation. The pyridine-containing bicyclic structure mimics Axin scaffolding interactions, preventing β-catenin nuclear translocation and subsequent TCF/LEF-dependent gene transcription in hair follicle stem cells.
candidates.structural_rationale: Novel pyridine-piperidine hybrid scaffold with isobutylaryl substituent distinguishes from existing GSK3β inhibitors (e.g., LiCl, CHIR99021) by incorporating both hydrogen bond donors (secondary amide) and π-stacking capability through heteroaromatic cores. This design targets the Axin-binding pocket rather than ATP-competitive GSK3β inhibition, reducing off-target kinase effects and improving hair follicle selectivity.
candidates.novelty_assessment: No prior literature reports this specific pyridine-piperidine-anilide scaffold for Wnt inhibition in AGA context. Differs from known compounds by: (1) indirect GSK3β modulation via Axin interaction rather than direct kinase inhibition, (2) incorporation of heteroaromatic stabilizing elements absent in current therapeutics, (3) structural design optimized for follicular penetration rather than systemic delivery. The absence of research reflects gap in non-kinase-based Wnt pathway targeting.

candidates.predicted_moa: Tankyrase inhibitor preventing Axin ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. By blocking TNKS1/2-mediated PARylation of Axin, this compound stabilizes the destruction complex, promoting β-catenin phosphorylation and degradation. Enhanced Axin levels suppress canonical Wnt signaling in dermal papilla cells critical for hair follicle maintenance.
candidates.structural_rationale: Bis-urea framework with morpholine tail represents structural departure from ATP-competitive TNKS inhibitors (e.g., XAV939). The symmetric urea linkages and extended conjugated system facilitate allosteric PARP-binding domain interaction. Morpholine moiety enhances solubility and follicle tissue penetration compared to lipophilic small molecules, while maintaining specificity for TNKS over PARP1/2.
candidates.novelty_assessment: Bis-urea-morpholine TNKS inhibitor design is novel for AGA treatment as TNKS pathway remains unexplored in androgenetic alopecia literature. Prior TNKS inhibitors (XAV939, IWR compounds) lack morpholine pharmacophore optimization for dermal delivery. This structural class has not been reported in hair biology, likely due to: (1) recent TNKS-Wnt connection elucidation, (2) developmental complexity of multi-target avoidance, (3) limited screening against follicle-specific phenotypes.

candidates.predicted_moa: Selective LRP6 co-receptor inhibitor blocking Wnt-Frizzled-LRP6 complex formation. This compound competitively displaces Axin from LRP6 phosphorylation sites through allosteric LRP6 ectodomain binding, preventing GSK3β recruitment and inhibiting canonical Wnt signaling. Particularly effective in suppressing Wnt3a/Wnt10b-induced proliferation in hair follicle stem and progenitor populations.
candidates.structural_rationale: Hindered biaryl structure with bulky tert-butyl groups and N,N-dimethylaniline tail creates steric barrier against LRP6 co-receptor engagement. Unlike β-catenin-targeting agents, this design targets the extracellular interaction interface via allosteric pocket near LRP6 LDLR domains. The phenolic hydroxyl and amide linker provide hydrogen bonding network mimicking Wnt ligand contacts, while lipophilicity enables membrane penetration and dermal accumulation.
candidates.novelty_assessment: LRP6-targeting approach for AGA is unexplored; published literature emphasizes intracellular Wnt inhibitors (GSK3β, Axin modulators). This extracellular targeting strategy offers: (1) reduced systemic toxicity versus intracellular pathway inhibition, (2) follicle-specific accessibility via dermal application, (3) mechanistic orthogonality to existing small molecules. Absence from literature reflects limited drug discovery focus on co-receptor modulation and challenges in validating extracellular protein-protein interaction inhibitors in follicle biology.

candidates.predicted_moa: Selective Androgen Receptor Degrader (SARD) - AR protein 분해 촉진을 통한 리간드-dependent 및 ligand-independent AR signaling 억제
candidates.structural_rationale: 기존 피나스테라이드는 5α-reductase 억제제이지만, 본 화합물은 PROTAC 유사 구조로 설계되어 AR 단백질 자체를 ubiquitin-proteasome pathway로 분해시킴. 스테로이드 골격과 isobutylphenyl-linker-carbamate 구조의 결합으로 AR ligand-binding domain (LBD) 결합 및 E3 ligase recruitment 이중 기능 제공
candidates.novelty_assessment: 기존 AR 억제제(bicalutamide, enzalutamide)는 ligand-competitive antagonist이나, SARD 메커니즘은 AR mRNA 수준을 감소시키고 constitutive-active AR 변이체도 억제 가능. 모발 여포의 dermal papilla cells에서 AR degradation은 androgen-induced miniaturization 역전에 효과적. 문헌 부재 이유: 모발 재생 분야에 SARD 적용은 미개척 영역

candidates.predicted_moa: Selective AR Modulator with Tissue-Selective Antagonism - 모낭 조직에서 AR 신호 차단, 전립선 조직에서는 부분적 활성 유지로 부작용 최소화
candidates.structural_rationale: 기존 non-steroidal AR antagonist와 달리, 비-스테로이드 구조(arylsulfonamide scaffold)로 설계하여 혈뇌장벽 투과성 감소 및 말초 조직 선택성 향상. Trifluoromethyl 치환과 urea linker는 hydrogen bonding network를 통해 모낭 특이적 AR 코팩터 단백질(HIC5, ARA55)과의 상호작용 증진. 이는 prostate vs dermal papilla cells 간 AR signaling 경로의 차이를 활용
candidates.novelty_assessment: 기존 bicalutamide, flutamide는 전신적 AR 차단으로 성기능 저하 등 부작용 야기. 본 화합물은 조직 특이적 코팩터 선택성을 통해 안드로겐 민감성 기관에는 영향 최소화. 모낭의 특수한 transcriptional context (specific AR-interacting protein profile)를 타겟하는 방식은 학술지에 미보고

candidates.predicted_moa: Allosteric Androgen Receptor Antagonist - AR N-terminal domain (NTD)와 ligand-binding domain (LBD) 간 interdomain communication 억제를 통한 비-경쟁적 AR 억제
candidates.structural_rationale: 기존 ligand-competitive antagonist와 달리, allosteric site (AR NTD의 AF-1 region 근처)를 타겟하는 새로운 스캐폴드. Hydroxyphenyl-carboxamide core와 pyridine linker, difluoromethyl 치환 조합으로 AF-2 site와는 직접 경쟁하지 않으면서도 AR 단량체 형성 및 DNA binding을 억제. 모낭 dermal papilla의 저 androgen 환경에서 baseline AR activity를 선택적으로 감소
candidates.novelty_assessment: Allosteric AR antagonism은 prostate cancer 분야에서도 초기 단계이며, 탈모 치료 목표로의 적용은 전무. 기존 orthosteric antagonist (enzalutamide)의 저항성 획득 (splice variant AR-V7 증가) 문제를 우회 가능. 비-선형 dose-response 특성으로 인해 off-target effects 감소 및 내성 개발 지연 가능성. 현재까지 모발 생물학 분야 문헌에 미존재하는 기전

candidates.predicted_moa: SRD5A2 competitive inhibitor targeting the steroid binding pocket through dual hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions with the enzyme's active site
candidates.structural_rationale: Novel sulfonamide-based scaffold incorporating: (1) lipophilic isobutylphenyl moiety for deep pocket penetration, (2) urea linker for enhanced H-bonding to Tyr91 and Asp99 residues in SRD5A2 active site, (3) pyridyl substituent for electrostatic interactions with enzyme backbone. Differs from finasteride by eliminating the 4-azasteroid core while maintaining potency through alternative binding geometry.
candidates.novelty_assessment: Novel heterocyclic sulfonamide-urea architecture not previously reported in SRD5A2 inhibitor literature. Deviates from classical steroid-based (finasteride, dutasteride) and azasteroid scaffolds. The combination of pyridine ring with sulfonamide linker represents unexplored chemical space for this target.

candidates.predicted_moa: Non-competitive allosteric SRD5A2 modulator binding to a secondary pocket distinct from the steroid-binding site, inducing conformational changes that reduce catalytic efficiency and substrate turnover
candidates.structural_rationale: Designed to access allosteric pocket via: (1) trifluoromethyl group providing lipophilic anchor and metabolic stability, (2) morpholine-glycine linker conferring flexibility for conformational fit, (3) hindered isobutylbenzamide moiety preventing direct active site competition. The methoxy-substitution pattern creates unique surface topology incompatible with classical steroidal binding but compatible with accessory binding pockets identified in SRD5A2 crystal structures.
candidates.novelty_assessment: First-in-class allosteric SRD5A2 inhibitor concept not yet explored in published literature. Unlike competitive inhibitors (finasteride, dutasteride) targeting the main active site, this scaffold exploits emerging structural biology data on SRD5A2 regulatory pockets. The morpholine-carbamate hybrid linker is structurally novel in context of 5-AR inhibition.

candidates.predicted_moa: Type II-selective SRD5A2 inhibitor via selective stabilization of the NAD(P)H-dependent catalytic cycle, with enhanced cofactor-dependent mechanism distinct from substrate-competitive inhibition
candidates.structural_rationale: Engineered for isoform-specific targeting through: (1) tetrahydroisoquinoline core providing unique 3D topology incompatible with SRD5A1 active site geometry while optimized for SRD5A2, (2) sulfonamide-difluorophenyl moiety targeting conserved serine/threonine residues unique to SRD5A2's cofactor binding interface, (3) isobutylbenzoyl group enhancing type II selectivity through hydrophobic interactions with SRD5A2-specific residues (Phe107, Val97). Selectivity advantage over finasteride (equipotent against both isoforms) achieved through differential cofactor stabilization.
candidates.novelty_assessment: Novel tetrahydroisoquinoline-sulfonamide scaffold representing unexplored chemical space in SRD5A2 literature. The isoform-selective mechanism based on cofactor interaction differentiation has not been previously reported. Difluorophenyl-sulfonamide linker combination is structurally distinct from existing inhibitors and provides novel handle for Type II selectivity optimization.

candidates.predicted_moa: 5α-Reductase Type 2 competitive inhibitor with enhanced androgen receptor binding affinity modulation. Mechanism involves direct NAD(P)H cofactor competition and selective Type 2 isoform inhibition through conformational stabilization of the enzyme's inactive state.
candidates.structural_rationale: This compound combines (1) a stereoselective bicyclic steroid core (derived from androsterone scaffold) that ensures proper 3D orientation for active site recognition, (2) an isoindoline amide linker providing hydrogen bonding networks for Type 2-specific recognition, and (3) an ibuprofen-like aromatic moiety enabling enhanced lipophilicity and cellular permeability. Unlike finasteride's azasteroid ring system, this design maintains native steroid backbone flexibility while introducing non-classical Type 2 selectivity through peripheral aromatic substitution.
candidates.novelty_assessment: Novel due to: (1) Hybrid small-molecule steroid conjugate approach not previously published in 5α-Reductase inhibitor literature, (2) Integration of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory pharmacophore with steroid core providing dual anti-inflammatory benefits in AGA context, (3) Avoidance of azasteroid core associated with sexual dysfunction side effects in published compounds, (4) Type 2 selectivity achieved through conformational locking rather than ring-system modification.

candidates.predicted_moa: Non-competitive allosteric inhibitor of 5α-Reductase Type 2 targeting an allosteric binding pocket distinct from the substrate binding site. Mechanism involves stabilization of the enzyme's C-terminal loop through σ-aromatic interactions, preventing necessary conformational changes for catalytic turnover without direct NAD(P)H interference.
candidates.structural_rationale: This quinolinone-based compound features (1) a methylenedioxy-substituted quinoline core enhancing metabolic stability and blood-brain barrier penetration, (2) a sulfonamide-linked piperidine linker providing pH-dependent conformational dynamics, (3) a bulky cyclohexyl substituent creating steric hindrance in the allosteric pocket, and (4) an unusual hydroxylated tetrahydrofuran amide side chain enabling water-soluble coordination sphere formation. This represents a mechanistically distinct approach from competitive inhibitors (finasteride, dutasteride), potentially reducing off-target effects.
candidates.novelty_assessment: Novel because: (1) Allosteric inhibition of 5α-Reductase Type 2 has not been extensively exploited in published literature, (2) Quinolinone scaffold applied to this target represents a new chemical class distinct from azasteroids and steroidal derivatives, (3) Multi-point conformational locking mechanism through C-terminal stabilization is structurally and mechanistically novel, (4) Integration of sulfonamide moiety addresses anti-inflammatory comorbidities in androgenetic alopecia.

candidates.predicted_moa: Mixed-type inhibitor of 5α-Reductase Type 2 combining competitive inhibition of NADPH binding pocket with Type 2-selective irreversible covalent modification through a latent electrophilic species. Mechanism involves Michael-type addition to a nucleophilic cysteine residue (Cys-98) unique to Type 2 isoform, ensuring long-duration inhibition and Type 2 selectivity.
candidates.structural_rationale: This compound incorporates (1) a 2,4,6-trimethyl-3-trifluoromethylphenyl aryl group providing exceptional Type 2 selectivity through steric discrimination of Type 1 active site geometry, (2) a cyclopentyl-pyrrolidone core creating a masked electrophilic intermediate activated by local protein environment, (3) a catechol moiety (3,4-dihydroxybenzene) enabling cofactor-mimetic interactions and chelation coordination, (4) conformational rigidity through pyrrolidone ring preventing off-target protein interactions. The trifluoromethyl group enhances metabolic stability while the catechol provides additional hydrogen bonding patterns.
candidates.novelty_assessment: Novel through: (1) Introduction of covalent inhibition mechanism to 5α-Reductase Type 2 field, reducing clinical dosing frequency compared to reversible inhibitors, (2) Pyrrolidone-based heterocyclic core provides unprecedented chemical class for this target, (3) Type 2-selective covalent mechanism targeting Cys-98 (absent in Type 1) ensures isoform selectivity without depending solely on pocket geometry, (4) Avoidance of published competitive inhibitor architectures while maintaining NADPH-mimetic features, (5) Catechol-based chelation chemistry represents unexplored coordination mode for steroid enzyme inhibition.

candidates.predicted_moa: β-catenin/TCF complex inhibitor via allosteric binding to β-catenin armadillo repeat domain, preventing interaction with TCF/LEF transcription factors and blocking Wnt/β-catenin signaling in hair follicle stem cells
candidates.structural_rationale: Incorporates indole moiety (hair follicle penetration) with isobutylaryl-substituted phenyl group for TCF-binding pocket interactions. The chiral amino acid scaffold provides structural rigidity and protein recognition capability absent in small molecule kinase inhibitors. Unlike finasteride's DHT-pathway targeting, this compound directly inhibits canonical Wnt signaling required for hair growth phase maintenance.
candidates.novelty_assessment: Novel scaffold combining indole-amino acid framework with aryl ketone pharmacophore. Not reported in literature due to: (1) lack of published screening data for β-catenin PPIs in alopecia context, (2) structural class distinctly different from GSK-3β inhibitors (CHIR99021-type) or tankyrase inhibitors, (3) target selectivity emphasizing β-catenin/TCF disruption over kinase pathways

candidates.predicted_moa: β-catenin stabilization inhibitor through targeting Axin-β-catenin complex assembly, promoting β-catenin proteasomal degradation and reducing canonical Wnt signaling hyperactivation in androgenetically-sensitized dermal papilla cells
candidates.structural_rationale: Methoxyindole scaffold with extended hydrophobic phenethyl and fluorobenzyl groups designed for Axin-binding interface disruption. The amide linkers provide conformational flexibility for penetrating protein-protein interaction surfaces. Differs from pyrvinium or IWP-2 by targeting stabilization complex rather than downstream secretion, offering reduced off-target effects on other Wnt-dependent tissues.
candidates.novelty_assessment: Novel heterocyclic PPI inhibitor combining indole core with bis-amide connectivity. Undiscovered in alopecia literature because: (1) Axin-recruitment mechanism not traditionally explored for hair disorders, (2) structural class orthogonal to GSK3β/APC pathway modulators dominating Wnt research, (3) selectivity for dermal papilla fibroblast context requires tissue-specific validation not yet reported

candidates.predicted_moa: Dual β-catenin/p300 CBP co-activator complex inhibitor, reducing transcriptional activation of LEF/TCF-responsive hair growth genes (CYCLIN D1, c-MYC) while attenuating androgen receptor cross-talk in hair follicle keratinocytes
candidates.structural_rationale: Acetamide-linked amino acid backbone with sulfonamide-substituted aniline for p300 binding pocket and tyrosine moiety for nuclear localization. N,N-dimethylaniline cap enhances cell permeability and nuclear accumulation. This structure simultaneously targets chromatin remodeling complex recruitment beyond simple β-catenin sequestration, providing synergistic suppression of AGA-accelerating transcription programs.
candidates.novelty_assessment: Novel hybrid PPI/epigenetic modulator combining protease-resistant amino acid scaffold with sulfonamide pharmacophore. Absent from literature due to: (1) lack of integrated approach targeting β-catenin AND co-activator function in follicle biology, (2) structural class (CBP/p300 inhibitors poorly explored for dermatological applications), (3) mechanistic focus on androgen receptor-Wnt crosstalk not previously characterized in AGA context
